PC: Listen to the patient heart and lungs.  Take vital signs.
If Patient has an arrhythmia they are treated with Electrical Cardio conversion/defibrillation or medication to correct the arrhythmia.
Oxygen is also given to the patient.

Thrombolytic therapy: This drug will attempt to break up the clot
Should not be used for people who have had a recent strokes, blood vessel abnormalities, intra cranial hemorrhage or recent head trauma.
Auscultate over the heart and listen for signs of heart failure like a 3rd or 4th heart sound.
Auscultate over the carotids and aorta and listen for bruits.  To make sure no there is no other atherosclerotic disease at these other sites.

Obtain a urine specimen to check for diabetes mellitus and renal disease
Since these are associated with accelerated MI

Obtain a blood specimen and check for lipids, glucose, hematocrit, and Thyroid function
This also may accelerate or explain the chest pain
Obtain a Chest X RAY.  May show cardiac enlargement, ventricular aneurysm,  or other signs of heart failure
Obtain an ECG.  Can give you indication as to if there has been ischemic heart disease or not.
IV line for fluids and medications

Once a full diagnosis of MI has been made one treatment pathway is to complete a percutaneous coronary intervention.
This is the process of angioplasty and stenting to open the coronary arteries and allow blood flow back to the heart.

Medications to prescribe
Anti Platelet therapy(Aspirin) : A blood thinner that will reduce the chance of blood being blocked in the coronary artery
Nitric Oxide: to treat minor events of chest pain.  Will lead to venodilation and pain reduction.
Beta Blockers: they reduce myocardial oxygen demand by lowering heart rate and contractility
Calcium Channel blockers: vasodilator
MK: Patients with abnormal ECG may need additional imaging such as arteriography, CT, or ultrasound.
ICS:
Once treatments have been administered it will be important to counsel the patient on the healthy lifestyle and exercise in order to prevent this occurring again.
A lipid reducing drug may be prescribed to decrease atherosclerotic plaque
If patient smokes make sure to counsel on the dangers of smoking and the benefits of quitting.
